name: US inflation
summary: US CPI about 4.1% a year in October by the FRED index, up from 4.0% and rising for three months
state: The FRED CPI index puts annual US inflation at 4.08% in October, up from 4.02% in September and rising for a third month, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band (FRED). Data released on 10 Nov showed headline and core prices rising faster than forecast, and markets moved to price a Federal Reserve rate rise in December (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov). The November CPI report is due in mid-December.
for_you: Higher prices for food, rent, transport and energy squeeze real incomes, especially for lower-income households. Borrowing costs tend to stay high or rise while inflation runs above target.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.08% within 3.0–4.5% Watch band and rising for 3 consecutive months

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.
